purpose: Original bounded design notes, with documented behavior separated from proposed Ultra limits. No runtime parity claim.

zl_shared.ports: All selected zl help instances save two inlets and two outlets. Some mode-specific XML marks an input or output inactive; keep saved topology separate from active roles.

attributes.zlmaxsize: Changes maximum retained list length; 256 default and 32767 maximum are documented in the family reference.
attributes.fuzzy: Comparison epsilon is named, but the installed per-mode prose and default are placeholders.

zl_shared.reset_distinction: Family XML says zlreset preserves mode parameters that zlclear zeroes for iter, nth, rot, slice and sort; group size survives either reset. Mode-specific reset descriptions are often placeholders.
bounded_ultra_proposal: Start with independent fixed-mode kinds accepting at most eight typed atoms; reject over-capacity input explicitly before mutating state.
Keep the existing message type, selector, atom tags and 31-byte ASCII symbol limits explicit. Eight atoms is an Ultra proposal, not a Max list limit.
Reserve both saved ports even when a role is inactive. Do not change saved cable indexes when adding an adapter.
Defer runtime mode switching, fuzzy comparison, dynamic capacity and family-wide reset behavior until matching original scores exist.
Capture symbols that head a message separately from numeric lists and explicit symbol messages; do not assume all selectors are data.
acceptance_requirements: Record typed outlet events in global order with console diagnostics.
Exercise empty input, scalar, one-item list, mixed symbols/numbers, bang before input and after clear.
Probe synchronous feedback/reentrancy with a bounded event budget; an immediate burst has no scheduler delay.
Inspect cold edits followed by bang, and distinguish recalculation from simple replay per mode.

input_roles: 0: scalar or list input; bang recalls.

iter.arguments_and_defaults: No functional creation argument is established. XML contains a required OBJARG_NAME template, while help saves bare iter instances.
behavior: Numeric scalars pass through. A list emits its elements consecutively in source order.
Bang emits the most recently received number/list again. Anything is linked to list handling in the method reference.
bounded_contract: Implement an immediate one-in/one-out iterator over at most eight typed atoms, preserving atom tags and downstream completion before the next atom.
Store the accepted input for bang recall; reject excess length atomically.
gaps: XML list wording names numbers, while anything delegates to list; symbol-head behavior and explicit symbol output selectors need a score.
Empty list, bang before input, feedback during a burst and whether feedback replaces the active iteration buffer are unmeasured.
acceptance_cases: Send a distinct mixed list, then bang; capture each atom's selector and order.
During the first atom's downstream processing, send a new list back into iter and inspect outer-burst continuation.

input_roles: 0: destination-tagged numeric list or offset command.
output_roles: 0..N-1: numeric element or list selected by the leading index.

spray.arguments_and_defaults: Outlet count defaults to 2, numbering offset to 0, and listmode to 0. The third argument 1 sends the complete payload list to one selected outlet.
behavior: Default mode uses the first number as an outlet index and sends following numbers to consecutive outlets, delivering rightmost outputs first.
Symbols in the ordinary distribution list are ignored. A bare int reports an error rather than routing.
Leading -1 broadcasts remaining values to all outlets; exact interaction with offset/listmode is unmeasured. offset changes outlet numbering.
bounded_contract: Support 1..8 outputs, explicit initial offset and ordinary numeric distribution first.
Validate the entire addressed range before output; capture Max's actual out-of-range behavior before claiming compatibility.
Add listmode and -1 broadcast as separately tested options, with bounded event expansion.
gaps: Symbols, invalid/fractional outlet indexes, negative offsets, overlong payloads and index -1 with nonzero offset need an oracle.
Whether ignored symbols consume destination positions and broadcast ordering are not settled by the prose.
acceptance_cases: Send a three-number payload starting at an interior outlet and record descending outlet order.
Compare bare int, symbol-containing list, -1 broadcast and listmode 1 across offsets 0 and 2.

input_roles: 0..N-1: replace the pending message for this inlet; left clear resets pending data.
output_roles: 0..N-1: corresponding stored message when every inlet has arrived.

behavior: Each inlet records an arrival. Once all have arrived, messages leave the corresponding outlets from right to left, and a fresh round begins.
Bang is interpreted as numeric 0. int, float, list and anything arrivals are documented.
clear in the left inlet deletes stored values.
bounded_contract: Use 2..8 slots with a readiness bitmask and one owned typed message per slot.
Snapshot a complete ready round before beginning right-to-left downstream delivery; establish reentrant semantics with Max before accepting feedback.
Define clear as a tested reset of both data and readiness; do not merely zero the values.
gaps: Repeated arrivals at one inlet before the others, readiness reset timing and reentrant arrivals during output need observation.
Whether clear affects only data or readiness as well is not explicitly spelled out by the method prose.
acceptance_cases: Send two values to inlet 0 before inlet 1, then repeat a second round; capture latest-value selection and ordering.
Partially fill, clear, then complete only the formerly missing inlet and verify whether output occurs.
Compare bang arrival with integer 0 and explicit symbol/list messages.

input_roles: 0..N-1: data, bang recall or silent set.
output_roles: 0: list beginning with the inlet index plus offset.

funnel.arguments_and_defaults: Optional inlet count defaults to 2; optional index offset defaults to 0.
behavior: Incoming numbers produce an index/value list. Lists gain an index atom, retaining floats within lists.
Bang recalls the most recently stored number for that inlet, with its inlet index.
offset changes numbering. set accepts a numeric list without output; its wording suggests setting per-inlet numeric storage.
bounded_contract: Use 2..8 inputs and index-tagged scalar/list output whose total size remains within eight atoms.
Begin with numeric scalar storage, per-inlet bang recall and offset. Add arbitrary lists only after selector/storage semantics are pinned.
Reject an input whose prepended tag would exceed capacity before changing state.
gaps: Scalar float-to-int behavior is not explicitly settled; the list entry specifically promises no float-to-int conversion.
Bang after a list, initial stored values, symbol-headed anything and set distribution from a non-left inlet need runtime cases.
acceptance_cases: Send scalar float then a mixed numeric/symbol list at a nonzero inlet; bang that inlet after each.
Send set with fewer/equal/more values than inputs, then bang every inlet; repeat with a nonzero offset.

input_roles: 0..N-1: store scalar/list segments; configured trigger inputs emit; bang emits from any inlet.
output_roles: 0: concatenation of all stored segments in inlet order.

join.arguments_and_defaults: Inlet count defaults to 2 with two initial integer-zero items, despite optional=0 argument metadata. The default triggers attribute value is not stated by installed XML.
behavior: Each inlet stores an untyped scalar or a variable-length segment; trigger inlets emit the whole concatenation.
Anything stores its selector and arguments as part of a segment. set stores without output.
Bang at any inlet emits current segments. triggers lists hot inlet indexes; -1 selects every inlet.

attributes.triggers: Writable/readable integer index list, declared size 256; -1 makes all inputs hot. Default is not documented in metadata.

bounded_contract: Introduce a new message-join kind distinct from Ultra's existing join registry key, which represents join~ audio.
Use 2..8 segments and at most eight output atoms total; require an explicit trigger set initially.
Validate complete concatenation size before mutation or emission; preserve typed segments and silent set.
gaps: Missing triggers default, zero/one inlet counts, segment growth, empty segments and bang from cold inputs need scores.
Creation syntax and trigger indexing must be tested independently from audio join~.
acceptance_cases: Store two multi-atom segments cold, then bang each inlet; verify concatenation order.
Compare explicit triggers 0, triggers 1 and triggers -1; set a hot segment silently.
Attempt combined payload length nine in an eight-atom Ultra profile and verify atomic refusal.

input_roles: 0: input to prefix; set changes prefix silently.

prepend.arguments_and_defaults: Documented creation prefix starts with a required symbol. Missing-prefix behavior is unestablished. Constructed messages have a documented maximum of 256 items.
behavior: A retained prefix is placed before incoming data. set replaces the prefix without output.
Bang is described as appending the bang word to the retained message; the method sentence is malformed and needs a reference capture.
bounded_contract: Support a nonempty symbol-led prefix and a combined payload within the existing eight-atom message profile.
Preserve selector versus symbol/list distinctions, and implement silent prefix replacement.
Do not count the native selector field as a data atom without defining a precise conversion rule.
gaps: Bang handling, no prefix, numeric prefix via set, empty set and total-item counting need scores.
The int/float entries refer to a stored integer/float despite a symbol-first creation argument; do not infer lexical output type.
acceptance_cases: Use an original symbol prefix with numeric, explicit symbol, list and anything input; inspect selector plus all atoms.
Replace the prefix via set, send bang, then compare empty and numeric replacement prefixes.

input_roles: 0: data to suffix; set changes retained message silently; bang recalls.

append.arguments_and_defaults: Optional suffix message. Help saves a no-argument instance; XML gives no explicit initial suffix value.
behavior: The retained suffix follows incoming int, float, list or anything data.
set replaces retained message without output. Bang is documented as emitting the most recently stored message, including after set.
bounded_contract: Use an explicit initial suffix and a combined eight-atom typed-message capacity.
Keep bang recall distinct from prepending a literal bang word, subject to a new Max oracle.
Validate replacement and output size atomically.
gaps: After ordinary input, the reference does not unambiguously distinguish recall of suffix, last input or last combined output.
Empty suffix, symbol-led suffix, bare symbol input and overflow need typed traces.
acceptance_cases: Send data A with suffix B, then bang; distinguish A B, B and any literal bang output.
Send set with a new suffix, bang, numeric input, explicit symbol and selector-led message.

input_roles: 0: store and evaluate, bang evaluate, list distribute; other inputs store variable values.

expr.arguments_and_defaults: A required C-like expression references $i1..$i9, $f1..$f9 and $s1..$s9. Unset variable values evaluate as 0. Sparse variable indexes and constant-only inlet count need capture.
behavior: Numeric input stores values; integer references truncate fractional inputs. Left input evaluates, other inputs are cold.
A left list updates successive variables then evaluates; set performs the distribution silently. Missing list items preserve prior values.
Documented grammar includes arithmetic, logical/bitwise operations, math functions, random/noise and table reads/writes through symbolic references.
bounded_contract: Parse a bounded expression grammar into a validated native representation; never use JavaScript eval or a general shell/interpreter.
First support 1..8 numeric variables, finite constants, arithmetic and explicit int/float casts; cap source length, AST nodes and evaluation steps.
Reject tables, random/noise, external functions and unsupported operators before graph admission. Retain expression text separately from generic literal-message parsing.
Specify domain, divide-by-zero and overflow handling from Max traces before claiming compatible results.
gaps: Output int/float inference, integer division/overflow width, evaluation order and domain failures need observation.
The authoring parser currently rejects dollar signs, quotes, escapes and commas used by the expression syntax.
A bounded numeric expression subset cannot be described as support for tables, random functions or extension code.
acceptance_cases: Compare integer and float variables, cold updates, short lists, set followed by bang, and sparse indexes.
Capture negative integer division/modulo, zero division, sqrt of a negative value and mixed cast expressions with console diagnostics.

regexp.arguments_and_defaults: Optional PCRE expression and substitution. binary defaults disabled in prose. New objects use the corrected Max 9.1 output order; old saved patches retain legacy behavior. XML does not state default re, substitute or tosymbol values.
behavior: Numbers and symbol/list messages become a subject string; configured expressions find substrings/captures and may substitute using percent-number references.

re sets the expression. substitute with no symbol removes the replacement. tosymbol 0 interprets output atoms, 1 preserves substituted output as a symbol, and 2 also preserves captures/substrings as symbols.
binary changes processing to byte lists and adds structured count/group/done output sequences.
legacyoutputorder preserves the former left-to-right ordering of captures versus substrings for legacy patches; new instances use the corrected order.

attributes.binary: 0 text by default; 1 byte processing, with values outside 0..255 converted to 0 except capture references.
attributes.legacyoutputorder: Saved compatibility flag introduced in 9.1.0; legacy/new object context matters.
attributes.re: PCRE expression string; Max quoting and backslash handling precede regex parsing.
attributes.substitute: Replacement string using percent-number capture references; empty command removes it.
attributes.tosymbol: Output modes 0, 1 or 2; initial value is not explicitly documented here.

bounded_contract: Keep as a research-only candidate until a compatible regex engine and bounded resource/step policy are selected.
An eventual subset should declare supported PCRE syntax, subject/pattern/replacement sizes, output count and UTF-8 policy explicitly.
Do not substitute JavaScript RegExp and claim PCRE parity. Separate saved legacy ordering from new-object defaults.
Keep regex work off audio execution paths and make compilation/match failure observable.
gaps: Engine version, match/recursion limits, invalid-pattern diagnostics, empty matches and full cross-outlet order need capture.
Current 31-byte ASCII symbols and literal parser cannot represent the documented quoting, backslashes, UTF-8 and replacement grammar.
Binary mode emits a protocol beyond simple text substitutions and requires separate acceptance work.
acceptance_cases: Use a finite literal pattern with one capture, two matches and a replacement; capture every outlet for new and legacy flags.
Compare tosymbol 0/1/2 on leading-zero strings, no-match input, invalid expression and empty-width matches.
Capture byte-list count/group/done sequences separately from text mode.

input_roles: 0: collect atoms; bang emits partial group.

zl.group.arguments_and_defaults: Optional group size; no numeric size default is stated in the inspected argument row. zlmaxsize uses the family 256 default.
behavior: Accumulate atoms across inputs, output groups of the configured size and retain remaining atoms.
Left bang immediately emits the current list. zlclear clears retained items; family reference says group size survives both clear and reset.
bounded_contract: Require explicit group size 1..8 and a fixed eight-atom carry buffer; consume long accepted inputs incrementally without overflowing that buffer.
Complete each downstream group delivery before the next group. Capture bang consumption and reentrancy before implementing partial flush.
gaps: No-argument size, size zero/negative, shrinking a partially collected group and whether bang consumes partial contents need scores.
acceptance_cases: For size 3, send 2 atoms then 5 atoms; inspect both full groups and the residual.
Bang a partial group twice, change size with residual pending, and compare zlclear with zlreset.

input_roles: 0: list to split into successive chunks.
output_roles: 0: chunks in source order, final chunk may be shorter.

zl.iter.arguments_and_defaults: Optional initial chunk size; numeric default is not stated. Family capacity default is 256.
behavior: Emit a sequence of lists of the configured size; the final list retains any shorter remainder.
Bang repeats previous output according to the method digest; whether that means the complete chunk sequence needs a runtime trace.
bounded_contract: Require chunk size 1..8 and input up to eight typed atoms; emit each chunk synchronously.
Keep iter's scalar-atom contract separate from zl.iter's chunked-list contract.
gaps: Bang after cold size change, scalar chunk selector, zero/negative size and reentrant buffer changes need capture.
acceptance_cases: Chunk a seven-atom mixed list by 3; verify 3/3/1 output and atom tags.
Change chunk size cold then bang, and compare with a fresh input.

zl.reg.arguments_and_defaults: Optional initial stored list; empty/no-initial-list output behavior is not stated.
behavior: The hot input stores and emits a list; the right input replaces it without output. Bang recalls retained content.
bounded_contract: Use an owned eight-atom typed list with hot/cold replacement and bang recall.
Keep no-value and empty-list state explicit instead of inventing an initial integer-zero list.
gaps: Bang before input, explicit empty list, symbol-headed anything and bang after clear need an oracle.
acceptance_cases: Seed an original mixed list, replace cold, bang hot and clear; inspect silence and typed output separately.

zl.join.arguments_and_defaults: Optional initial right-side list; no explicit missing-list value is stated.
behavior: Hot list input emits the two concatenated segments. Cold input sets the right segment. Bang requests current concatenation.
bounded_contract: Store two typed segments with at most eight combined atoms; reject overflow atomically.
Keep fixed hot/cold roles and two saved outputs distinct from message join's configurable trigger inputs.
gaps: Bang following a cold replacement, empty segments and selector-to-list conversion need scores.
acceptance_cases: Set a right segment cold, send a hot segment, replace right cold and bang; verify recomputation rather than stale recall.

zl.len.arguments_and_defaults: No functional creation arguments are listed. Family maximum retained length defaults to 256.
behavior: The family reference defines output as the number of list elements. Per-mode description and several method descriptions are placeholders.
bounded_contract: Count typed atoms in an accepted list up to eight atoms while retaining the saved two-in/two-out shape.
Define bang recall only after observing the family replay rule on this mode.
gaps: Scalar, explicit symbol, selector plus arguments, empty list, bang-before-input and clear behavior are undocumented at useful per-mode detail.
acceptance_cases: Compare numeric scalar, three atoms, explicit list, symbol and anything with two arguments; record count and diagnostics.

input_roles: 1: one-based index, optionally followed by replacement data.
output_roles: 1: source with item removed, or optional substitution result.

zl.nth.arguments_and_defaults: Optional initial one-based index, optionally with replacement. No numeric initial-index default is stated.
behavior: Extract the indexed item. A right-inlet index/replacement list configures replacement in the second output.
Bang repeats prior output according to the per-mode digest.
bounded_contract: Begin with explicit index 1..8, no substitution, and both extracted-item and remainder outputs.
Capture cross-outlet order and all invalid-index policies before runtime implementation.
gaps: Index zero/negative/out-of-range, replacement length, default index and cold edit plus bang need capture.
Port label describes removal while the argument/method rows describe optional substitution; model these as separate modes.
acceptance_cases: Extract first/middle/last from a mixed list, then compare index 0 and beyond length.
Configure a replacement via the right input and capture both outputs and order.

zl.slice.arguments_and_defaults: Optional positive slice size; its numeric default is not stated.
behavior: Split at the configured item count. Emit the tail from the right outlet before the leading slice from the left.
Bang requests previous output; cold-size interaction remains unmeasured.
bounded_contract: Require an explicit size 1..8 and source length at most eight; preserve right-to-left output delivery.
Capture empty-side emission and size beyond input length before defining those cases.
gaps: Size zero/negative/beyond source, empty lists and bang after a cold change need capture.
acceptance_cases: Split five mixed atoms at 2, then 5 and 7; inspect empty-tail representation and global outlet order.

zl.rev.arguments_and_defaults: No functional argument is established; OBJARG_NAME is a template, not a required argument specification.
behavior: Reverse the incoming list's atom order. Family mode prose supplies the behavior missing from the per-mode description.
The bang digest requests previous output.
bounded_contract: Reverse at most eight typed atoms without changing their tags; keep both saved ports with inactive roles documented.
gaps: Scalar/empty input, selector-led anything, recall state and reset behavior need reference scores.
acceptance_cases: Reverse an asymmetric mixed list, bang, clear and bang; verify values, selectors and silence.

zl.rot.arguments_and_defaults: Optional integer distance; positive moves right and negative moves left. Numeric default is not stated.
behavior: Rotate atoms by the configured signed distance. A right-inlet integer updates the distance.
Bang digest requests previous output; family reset prose distinguishes clearing the mode parameter from retaining it.
bounded_contract: Use an explicit signed distance and at most eight atoms; retain typed atoms and fixed saved topology.
Measure distances larger than list length before choosing modulo normalization.
gaps: No-argument distance, large distances, empty input and whether repeated bang rotates again or replays need scores.
acceptance_cases: Rotate five distinct atoms by 2, -2, 0 and 7; bang twice after a cold distance update.

zl.sort.arguments_and_defaults: Optional sort direction: -1 descending, all other values ascending. No numeric initial argument default is stated.
behavior: Sort data and also emit the reordered index list. Right input changes sort direction.
Bang repeats prior output according to its digest.
bounded_contract: Begin with finite numeric lists up to eight atoms and explicit order 0 or -1.
Emit both sorted values and source-index mapping only after index base, tie stability and outlet ordering are captured.
Reject mixed symbol/numeric sorting until Max's comparison order is established.
gaps: Index base, equal-key stability, int/float ties, symbol collation and multi-outlet order are unspecified here.
fuzzy comparison metadata does not establish sort semantics or default epsilon.
acceptance_cases: Sort repeated numeric values with distinguishable int/float tags in both directions; inspect index mapping.
Compare all-symbol and mixed-symbol lists and cold direction plus bang.

input_roles: 0: add items; bang removes oldest; clear resets.

zl.queue.arguments_and_defaults: No queue-specific argument is listed; family maximum list length defaults to 256.
behavior: Bang emits and removes the oldest retained item. The second outlet reports the number of queued items.
zlclear empties retained items. Data method prose contains placeholders, so multi-atom input granularity is unresolved.
bounded_contract: Require an explicit eight-atom FIFO capacity; use typed scalar items first, with no delayed clock semantics.
Overflow must refuse the new data atomically with explicit status and preserve queued items.
Add count output only after enqueue/dequeue/clear timing and order are measured.
gaps: Whether a list queues one message or several atoms, empty-queue bang behavior, count emission timing and capacity overflow need scores.
The family overview says messages while the method/port descriptions say items; do not equate this with pipe's scheduled message snapshots.
acceptance_cases: Enqueue three scalars, then a two-item list, bang to exhaustion and one extra time; retain data/count/diagnostics.
Clear partially filled storage and test count output plus bang.

output_roles: 0: latest N atoms once full, repeated after later arrivals.

zl.stream.arguments_and_defaults: Per-mode metadata requires an initial length, but help also saves a bare zl stream instance outside the selected basic anchor. No-argument length is unestablished. Negative length reverses output.
behavior: Collect a sliding window. Once its size is reached, emit it after each later input, with a readiness flag indicating the full state.
Negative length requests reversed window order. zlclear resets collected data.
bounded_contract: Require explicit window length 1..8 initially, a fixed ring buffer and both data/readiness outputs.
Begin with one scalar per input; separately capture multi-atom input emission granularity, readiness timing and output order.
Treat reverse windows and size changes as separately tested extensions.
gaps: Family prose describes readiness as length-defined; per-mode description says length-reached. Use runtime evidence to settle timing.
Per-mode output labels hard-code 256 despite variable length; these are stale labels rather than a fixed window contract.
Zero length, negative length, shrinking/growing live windows, bang before full and list input granularity need scores.
acceptance_cases: For window 3, send five scalars and inspect warmup flags plus three successive windows.
Compare a single five-atom list with five scalar arrivals; then change size, clear and bang.
